import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Error: 'data/dogs_zurich.csv' not found. Please ensure the dataset is in the correct directory.")
    exit()

# --- Data Preparation ---

# Drop rows where the primary breed is not specified
df.dropna(subset=['Rasse1Text'], inplace=True)

# Clean up breed names: handle common mixed-breed variations
df['Rasse1Text'] = df['Rasse1Text'].replace({
    'Mischling klein': 'Mischling',
    'Mischling mittel': 'Mischling',
    'Mischling gross': 'Mischling'
})

# Identify the top 10 most popular breeds across all years
top_10_breeds = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(10).index

# Filter the DataFrame to include only the top 10 breeds
df_top_breeds = df[df['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_10_breeds)].copy()

# Aggregate the data: count the number of dogs for each breed in each year
breed_trends = df_top_breeds.groupby(['StichtagDatJahr', 'Rasse1Text']).size().reset_index(name='count')

# --- Visualization ---

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="colorblind")

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the line plot showing trends for each breed
lineplot = sns.lineplot(
    data=breed_trends,
    x='StichtagDatJahr',
    y='count',
    hue='Rasse1Text',
    style='Rasse1Text',
    markers=True,
    dashes=False,
    linewidth=2.5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---

# Set title and labels with improved formatting
ax.set_title(
    'Popularity of Top 10 Dog Breeds in Zurich Over Time',
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight='bold',
    pad=25
)
ax.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Customize tick parameters for better readability
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12)

# Ensure x-axis ticks are integers
ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(integer=True))
plt.xticks(rotation=0)

# Improve the legend
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax.legend(
    handles=handles,
    labels=labels,
    title='Dog Breed',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    fontsize=11,
    title_fontsize=13
)

# Add a subtle grid and remove unnecessary spines
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
sns.despine(left=True, bottom=True)

# Add a source text annotation for context
plt.figtext(0.99, 0.01, 'Source: Open Data Zurich, Dog Registrations',
            horizontalalignment='right',
            fontsize=9,
            color='gray')

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95]) # Adjust rect to make space for figtext and title

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
